title: Order cancellation
scope: The backend order lifecycle and its event publication, for the task `Research how orders change state and what cancelling one would touch`. The web client's order views were out of scope.
problem: Customers cannot cancel an order once it is placed. Support staff cancel orders by editing the database row, which skips the order-changed event and leaves the warehouse queue unaware.
asks: A customer can cancel their own order while it is ACTIVE.
The warehouse learns about a cancellation without a manual step.

files.purpose: Every order state change goes through OrderService.
Persists orders; the only writer of the orders table.
Publishes domain events to the warehouse queue.

patterns.name: Ownership check, then transition
patterns.description: The refund flow loads the order, rejects a caller who does not own it, checks the current status, then saves and publishes. A cancellation would follow the same order of checks.

data_flow.step: The router calls `OrderService.refund` with the session user.
The service saves the new status.
The service publishes `order.refunded`, which the warehouse consumer reads.

dependencies.name: @aws-sdk/client-sqs
dependencies.role: Carries domain events to the warehouse queue.

dependencies.name: src/events
dependencies.role: Wraps queue publishing for every domain event.

external.fact: `MessageGroupId` is required for every message sent to a FIFO queue.
external.consequence: A cancellation event must carry the order id as its message group, the way `publish` already sets it for refunds, or SQS rejects it.

approaches.name: New cancel transition in OrderService
approaches.concept: Add a cancel method beside refund that checks ownership and ACTIVE status, saves CANCELLED, and publishes `order.cancelled`.
pros: Keeps every state change in one service.
cons: The warehouse consumer must learn a new event type.

approaches.name: Generic status endpoint
approaches.concept: Expose one endpoint that sets any allowed status from a transition table.
cons: Moves validation into a table the tests do not cover.

recommendation: Add the cancel transition to `OrderService`, following `refund`.

open_questions.question: May a customer cancel an order after it has shipped?

options.label: No, only before shipping
options.description: Matches the refund flow, which rejects orders in the wrong state.

options.label: Yes, as a return request
options.description: Needs a new RETURN_REQUESTED state and a warehouse notification.

sources.established: FIFO sends need MessageGroupId, which settles how the event is published.

lessons.lesson: Status changes must go through the service, because the repository does not publish events.

not_covered: The web client's order views, which consume the same events.
next_steps: Research the warehouse consumer in the `warehouse` repo.
